title: From Adam to Noah

lettering_types.caption: Narration box
lettering_types.divine: God's words: Cinzel on solid dark band, no speaker drawn

world_rule: Setting rule for Genesis 5: open lands, simple tents of hide and early stone dwellings only. Implements only of plain wood or stone; no metal tools, no plows, no wheels.

panels.camera: medium, Adam (mature, grey at the temples) looking over his fields at sunrise

text.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.

panels.camera: medium, Adam holding a small child whose face is turned toward him; the child's face is hidden
panels.art: Adam with his young son Seth.

text.text: Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and became the father of a son in his own likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.

panels.camera: medium, Adam very old with long white hair and beard, seated at dusk at the door of a hide tent
panels.art: Adam at the end of his long life.

text.text: All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.

panels.camera: wide, Enoch walking along a hill path at sunrise, children and grandchildren around his tent below

text.text: After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

panels.camera: wide, Enoch walking alone along a high hill toward a bright horizon, the low sun off to the side
panels.art: Enoch walking toward the light; no glow or halo around him.

panels.camera: the same hill and horizon, now empty, light lingering

text.text: and he was not found, for God took him.

panels.camera: close, Methuselah, extremely old, seated, looking out

text.text: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.

panels.camera: medium, Lamech in a field holding his newborn son wrapped in wool; the baby's face hidden

text.text: This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground which Yahweh has cursed.
text.speaker: LAMECH

panels.camera: medium, warm evening light, Noah seated with three small boys around him; the children's faces turned toward him
panels.art: Noah with his young sons Shem, Ham and Japheth.

text.text: Noah was five hundred years old, then Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

moral.heading: What This Story Teaches
moral.paragraph: Genesis 5 reads like a list of names, but it carries a message. Again and again it says “then he died,” showing that what God told Adam came true. Yet the line goes on, and in the middle of it stands Enoch, who “walked with God” (Genesis 5:24). Hebrews explains that before he was taken “he had been well pleasing to God” (Hebrews 11:5), and it says, “Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him” (Hebrews 11:6). The chapter ends with Noah, whose father hoped he would bring comfort (Genesis 5:29). Psalm 90:12 gives a fitting prayer: “teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.”
